bib.title: RAG+: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Application-Aware Reasoning

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "RAG+: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Application-Aware Reasoning", Yu Wang (first author; Xi'an Jiaotong Univ., internship at Huawei), Shiwan Zhao, Zhihu Wang, Ming Fan, Xicheng Zhang, Yubo Zhang, Zhengfan Wang, Heyuan Huang, Ting Liu. arXiv 2506.11555v4, 23 Sep 2025. The PDF states no venue, so call it preprint. Its format and "Ethics Statement" suggest an ACL-style submission, but that is my guess, not printed.

COVERAGE: All 25 pages and all 99,595 extracted chars were read, including the limitations, appendices A-C, Tables 9-15 and Figures 6-25. The reference list was skimmed. Extraction was clean text. Table 1 is slightly garbled in places (missing spaces, some "–" cells), and I checked those cells against the Table 10-12 duplicates.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. RAG+ keeps the normal retrieval step and attaches to each retrieved knowledge item a pre-aligned worked application example (a Q&A or reasoning chain showing the item in use). The pair goes into the prompt, with no retriever change and no fine-tuning.
 number: none
 setup: the knowledge-application alignment is built offline, in the construction stage
 quote: "Since the knowledge-application alignment is established offline, no modifications to retrieval or generation models are needed at inference."
 where: p5, Section 3.2
2. Headline gains of RAG+ over the matching non-augmented RAG variant, on accuracy.
 number: Qwen2.5-72B legal Rerank RAG 77.5 to Rerank RAG+ 87.5; LLaMA3.3-70B MedQA Rerank RAG 81.0 to 85.6 (the authors also say 85.6 against a 78.2 baseline)
 setup: multiple-choice sentencing prediction (CAIL2018, Article 234, 3 intervals, 200 samples); MedQA, 500 random samples, 4 options; Dify pipeline with BGE-M3 embeddings, top-3 chunks; average of 3 runs. Rerank RAG uses the same model to rerank the top 10 and keep 3. Ranges quoted in the abstract: average gains of 3-5%, peak 13.5%.
 quote: "In the legal domain, Qwen2.5-72B achieves 87.5% accuracy with Rerank RAG+, a 10% gain over its non-augmented version."
 where: p6, Section 5.2; Tables 2 and 3
 Note: the abstract's "peak gains up to 13.5%" is not matched by any single table-to-table delta I could find. The largest I found is 13.5 points for LLaMA3.3-70B AFRAG 41.5 to AFRAG+ 52.5, which is 11. GraphRAG LLaMA3.1-8B* 36.5 to 46.0 is 9.5. I could not locate 13.5 in the tables, so do not cite that figure as verified.
3. Plain RAG+ gains over plain RAG are often small. They are under 1 point for several models, and some cells go down.
 number: math 70.47 to 73.72 (Qwen2.5-72B); legal 76.5 to 83.0 (Qwen2.5-72B); MedQA Qwen2.5-7B 59.20 to 57.60 (a drop); LLaMA3.3-70B math 71.16 to 71.86
 setup: Tables 1-3. Math is a self-built Numerical Analysis set (430 questions, 816 knowledge points, 4-option multiple choice).
 quote: "Overall, most models achieve accuracy improvements between 2.5% and 6.5%, while the overall range spans from approximately 0.7% to 7.5%."
 where: p6, Section 5.1 (math); Tables 1-3
4. Application examples alone (no knowledge) help over baseline in most cases but underperform knowledge plus application.
 number: legal Qwen2.5-7B: RAG- (application only) 65.00, RAG 75.00, RAG+ 76.50; AFRAG- 34.50 (below baseline 46.00) and AFRAG+ 47.00
 setup: Table 6 (legal) and Table 7 (math); Table 13 (MedQA) is mixed, with RAG-app beating RAG+ for Qwen2.5-14B (70.60 vs 69.80)
 quote: "However, this setting still underperforms compared to the full configuration where both knowledge and application examples are included"
 where: p8, Section 5.5; Tables 6, 7, 13
5. A stronger reranker raises RAG+ more than RAG.
 number: legal Qwen2.5-7B: Rerank(72B) RAG 72.50 vs Rerank(72B) RAG+ 83.50; Rerank RAG 70.50 vs Rerank RAG+ 74.50
 setup: Table 4; reranker swapped for Qwen2.5-72B. On MedQA (Table 5) the gap is only 60.8 vs 61.8 for the 7B.
 quote: "Stronger reranking consistently improves accuracy across both tasks, with the largest gains in the Rerank (72B) RAG+ setting"
 where: p7, Section 5.4
6. Gains are uneven by model size, and the paper concedes diminishing returns for large models.
 number: LLaMA3.3-70B legal "marginal gains". Its own Table 2 contradicts this: RAG 70.5 to RAG+ 76.0, and Rerank RAG 77.5 to 77.5.
 quote: "indicating diminishing returns from retrieval augmentation as model size increases."
 where: p6, Section 5.2
7. GraphRAG often underperforms the baseline, and application augmentation recovers part of it.
 number: math GLM4-9B GraphRAG 33.95 vs baseline 46.51 (RAG+ variant 36.51); legal DS-Qwen-7B GraphRAG 42.0 vs baseline 53.0 (GraphRAG+ 47.5)
 setup: Tables 1 and 2. GraphRAG+ reuses the corpus applications via fuzzy matching. GraphRAG was omitted for MedQA because it was too expensive.
 quote: "GraphRAG without application augmentation can lead to performance drops."
 where: p6, Section 5.1
8. The open-ended legal setting shows small gains.
 number: Qwen2.5-7B 61.5 to 66.5; Qwen2.5-14B 75.5 to 76.5; Qwen2.5-72B 89.5 to 90.5
 setup: free-form sentence length; correct if it falls in the gold interval (Table 8)
 quote: "RAG+ consistently improves performance across all model sizes, demonstrating robustness even under open-ended evaluation."
 where: p8, Section 5.6; Table 8
9. Application corpus cost is modest.
 number: sizes grew from 223 KB to 612 KB (math), 528 KB to 868 KB (legal), 99,382 KB to 105,558 KB (medicine); about 6 hours to generate the medicine corpus with Qwen2.5-72B on eight 64 GB NPUs
 quote: "typically generating one to two examples per item"
 where: p9, Section 6
 Note: the sizes are the final corpus sizes as printed. I did not verify whether the "initial" figures mean the knowledge corpus alone.
10. Even with the right method retrieved, execution can fail.
 number: none
 setup: one case study (Qwen2.5-72B, Figure 5)
 quote: "even when the correct method is retrieved, symbolic reasoning may fail due to execution errors, highlighting the need for verification mechanisms alongside retrieval."
 where: p9, Section 5.7. Plausibly a point against that case's RAG answer, not RAG+.
11. How application examples are made. Two routes:
 Application generation: an LLM writes a worked example per item. Conceptual knowledge gets comprehension or analogy questions, procedural knowledge gets worked examples or reasoning chains. This was used for legal and medicine.
 Application matching: real problems are assigned to categories and matched to knowledge items by an LLM (Qwen2.5-72B, self-consistency voting), then refined by hand. This was used for math.
 quote: "knowledge points without matched real-world applications (under 10%) are supplemented with automatically generated examples."
 where: p5, Sections 3.1 and 4.2

LIMITS
- Authors concede (p9): building a high-quality application corpus can be resource-intensive, and LLM generation may introduce errors or oversimplify. Mismatched knowledge-application pairs can mislead. The work does not address retrieval quality or efficiency.
- Not shown: no comparison against retrieved few-shot examples chosen by query similarity (the pairing is per knowledge item, not per query). No comparison against simply putting more knowledge chunks in the prompt at equal token budget. No significance tests. Standard deviations appear only for the stochastic-decoding models; deterministic models report ±0.0, so the "3 runs" gives no variance for most cells.
- Small, self-built evaluation: the math set is built by the authors (430 questions), legal is 200 samples from a single article (Article 234, 3 interval options), MedQA is 500 samples. A 1-point gap is 2 questions on legal and 5 on MedQA.
- Application examples are generated by the same model family (Qwen2.5-72B) used in evaluation, so contamination is not ruled out. The medical examples are made from the MedQA training data and a textbook corpus.
- Rerank RAG+ needed re-prompting for format failures, and several cells are missing ("–").
- Dated: models are Qwen2.5, LLaMA3.x, DeepSeek-R1-distill and QwQ, all 2025-era. There are no frontier closed models.

BUILDS ON
Lewis et al. 2020 (RAG, NeurIPS); Asai et al. 2023 (Self-RAG, used for Answer-First RAG, ICLR); Edge et al. 2024 (GraphRAG, arXiv); Lin et al. 2023 (RA-DIT); Wang et al. 2024b (Re-TASK, capability items); Singh et al. 2025 (Agentic RAG); Xiong et al. 2025 (RAG-Gym); Zihao et al. 2024 (RAT); Islam et al. 2024 (Open-RAG, EMNLP Findings 2024); Ma et al. 2023 (Rewrite-Retrieve-Read); Bloom 2010 (taxonomy, "applying"); Anderson et al. 2004 (ACT-R, declarative vs procedural memory). Data: Jin et al. 2020 (MedQA); Xiao et al. 2018 and Zhong et al. 2018 (CAIL); Xiong et al. 2024 (medical corpus). Tools: BGE-M3, bge-reranker-v2-m3, Dify, vLLM (Kwon et al. 2023).

CODE: none in the paper. The RAG+ prompt skeleton, verbatim (Figure 13, p20), is worth keeping:
<Reference>
<Knowledge Point>
<Knowledge>
[Put One Knowledge Here]
</Knowledge>
<Applica�on>
[Put The Applica�on of the Knowledge Here]
</Applica�on>

...
<Reference>
Wrapper line: "Now use the reference knowledge and applications provided for guidance (but do not be strictly bound by them)". The extraction prints "Applica�on" with a garbled "ti" ligature.
Generation prompt for medicine (Figure 18, p22): "For procedural knowledge, please help me generate an example of using that procedural knowledge. All examples must be question-and-answer or multiple-choice questions."

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p1): Illustrative case of RAG vs RAG+. "At least one girl" combinatorics: RAG gives C(10,3)=120, RAG+ subtracts the all-boys case to get 100. Fastest explanation of the idea.
- Fig 2 (p4): Pipeline. (a) construction stage with generation vs matching; (b) inference stage, retrieve knowledge then its aligned application. This is the one to redraw.
- Fig 3 (p7): Conceptual vs procedural knowledge with their applications.
- Fig 4 (p7): Scaling 7B/14B/72B, Qwen2.5, RAG vs RAG+ and Rerank, legal and MedQA.
- Fig 5 (p8): Case study. RAG picks Lagrange interpolation and makes an algebra error; RAG+ follows a Newton divided-differences pattern.
- Figs 8-16 (pp18-21): Base/RAG/RAG+ prompt templates. Figs 17-19: application-generation prompts. Figs 20-25: examples.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. Table 1 and Table 3 have some garbled cells in the extraction (missing spaces, a "–" in Rerank RAG GLM4-9B and DS-Qwen-7B), resolved against Tables 10-12. The text calls "~81%" the LLaMA3.3-70B MedQA baseline, but Table 3 says 78.2. The text is also inconsistent about whether Qwen2.5-72B on legal Rerank RAG is 77.5 (Table 2) or the "10% gain" (87.5 - 77.5 = 10, which is consistent). Table 14 gives a different Qwen2.5-72B legal baseline (58.00) than Table 2 (73.00).

FIT TO THE NOTES (grep run)
- Strongest point: retrieval can return worked application examples paired with the facts, not only facts. Evidence is narrow and in-domain: the paired gain is a few points on average and unreliable at plain RAG level, and the application-only ablation shows facts still matter.
- Best home: 08-agentic-rag-prince.md, section "Retrieved few-shot examples" (line 393). That note's line 320 already says "retrieval used to *condition generation* rather than to supply answer content" for NL-to-SQL pairs. RAG+ differs in that the example is keyed to each fact rather than to the query, and is built offline. Natural addition: one sentence plus citation under that section, with the application-only ablation (legal 65.0 vs 75.0 vs 76.5) as the caveat.
- 06-generation-for-rag.md line 183 (table row "In-context learning | Retrieve examples of good past answers, not just facts") already states the claim without a source or number. That is a sharpens case. Cite RAG+ there.
- 02-why-rag-and-the-augmented-prompt.md (the ledger's target note): grep for "application", "worked example", "few-shot", "RAG+" and "Wang" turned up nothing on this idea. The closest is the augmented-prompt discussion and "What RAG buys you" (line 117). The note is about the prompt structure, so a one-sentence mention fits, but 08 or 06 is the better place.
- The ledger entry for 2506.11555 exists with status "downloaded", note target 02-why-rag-..., relevance 2. No note contains "2506.11555" or "RAG+" yet.
